# flue

> flue keeps your terminal sessions alive on the machine that owns them and hands them back on any device you have. A small Go daemon owns the shells and their scrollback; a web app renders them. Closing the tab detaches rather than kills, so a build, an agent run or an SSH session keeps going, and reattaching replays what was missed.

flue is open source (MIT), pre-1.0, and free. It installs as one static Go
binary on macOS, Linux and WSL, with no Node, Python or other toolchain.

There is no hosted service. The daemon binds loopback and nothing else.
Remote access is opt-in and runs on infrastructure you own: `flue relay setup`
deploys a relay Worker and the web app into your own Cloudflare account, on the
free tier. Traffic crossing that relay is end-to-end encrypted with Noise IK,
the daemon's static key pinned when a browser pairs, so the Worker forwards
ciphertext it holds no key for. flue.sh serves docs and downloads and is never
part of the data path.

Status: the local terminal, the login service, the fleet-wide sessions list and
the end-to-end pairing all work. The Cloudflare relay is built and deployable
but has not been through its manual end-to-end gate against a real account.
It is ready to try rather than ready to rely on.

## Install

```sh
brew install karnstack/tap/flue    # or: curl -fsSL https://flue.sh/install.sh | sh
flue enable
```

`flue enable` installs a login service, starts the daemon and opens the UI.
Everything after that happens in the browser.

## CLI

- `flue enable`: install the login service, start the daemon, open the UI
- `flue disable`: remove it
- `flue status`: daemon, login service and session diagnostics
- `flue open [path]`: spawn a session in a directory
- `flue serve`: run the daemon in the foreground, no login service
- `flue relay setup`: deploy a relay to your own Cloudflare account
- `flue relay join`: point this machine at a relay another machine deployed
- `flue relay status`: show the configured relay
- `flue relay update`: redeploy this release's relay; secret and pairings kept
- `flue relay address`: repoint this machine at a custom domain on the same relay

## Docs

- [How flue works](https://flue.sh/docs/how-it-works): the daemon that owns the shells, why closing a tab detaches rather than kills, how two devices mirror one session, and the CLI.
- [Remote access](https://flue.sh/docs/relay): how a machine becomes reachable from anywhere on infrastructure you own, the relay protocol, what it costs, and what a relay operator can and cannot see.
- [FAQ](https://flue.sh/docs/faq): short answers, including the one where the honest answer is not the flattering one. The web app's JavaScript is served by the relay origin, so a hostile origin is a real threat that encryption does not remove.

## Optional

- [Source](https://github.com/karnstack/flue): the repository. Everything is MIT licensed and there is no closed component.
- [The relay runbook](https://github.com/karnstack/flue/blob/main/docs/RELAY.md): operator-grade detail, the caps, and the counters.
- [The long FAQ](https://github.com/karnstack/flue/blob/main/docs/faq.md): the full version of the trust argument, including the exact move a hostile origin would make.
- [Developing flue](https://github.com/karnstack/flue/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md): the dev loop and the dev/prod split.
- [Relay protocol spec](https://github.com/karnstack/flue/blob/main/spec/relay-protocol.md): the normative protocol.
- [Known rough edges](https://github.com/karnstack/flue/blob/main/docs/FOLLOW-UPS.md): what is not finished.
